source.title: Do We Really Need a New Theory to Understand the Double-Descent?
source.authors: L. Oneto; S. Ridella; D. Anguita

record.tranche_reason: Tests double descent over model size using shallow polynomial and random-feature models, rather than the original deep-network settings.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own model-size sweeps and their training error, test/generalization error, Rademacher complexity, and algorithmic stability. The MNIST example is a shallow random-feature model, not a deep network. It does not sweep epochs or sample size. Results attributed to cited work are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study runs its own model-size sweeps and reports test error past the interpolation threshold. One sweep is a toy polynomial ridge regression. The other re-runs one of the Belkin et al. (arXiv:1812.11118) examples, a random-ReLU-feature least-squares classifier on MNIST, which is close to the original method. That bears on V4. The stability and Rademacher analyses are an explanatory argument, not a test of any version's prediction.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors argue that existing theory, specifically algorithmic (hypothesis) stability rather than capacity-based complexity, can explain the over-parameterized regime and double descent. They support this with two shallow-model examples and call for further theoretical and empirical work.
record.recipe_differences: The empirical method uses regularized least squares, a toy polynomial regression problem, and a shallow random-feature MNIST classifier; it does not reproduce the original deep-network settings.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper compares Rademacher complexity with algorithmic stability; the two measures give different accounts of the post-interpolation regime.

fits_no_version.finding: Hypothesis-stability estimates fall after the interpolation threshold. The stability-based bound selects the second minimum (p=16) in the toy model, while the Rademacher-based bound selects p=2, since Rademacher complexity only grows with p. MNIST is said to confirm this.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Algorithmic-stability-based generalization bounds track the second descent, while capacity-based bounds (Rademacher) predict only the classical U-shape.

record.peer_reviewed: The European Symposium on Artificial Neural Networks proceedings
record.problems: The empirical examples are shallow models rather than deep networks. The authors report a single round for the toy example, saying results are consistent over repetitions and parameter changes, but provide no uncertainty estimates. Numerical curve values are shown only in figures.

untested.parts: No deep networks; the authors restrict their analysis to shallow models.
No sweep over epochs or training time.
Only two shallow settings: polynomial basis and random ReLU features. Other model classes are not tested.
No single measure is used to predict the peak location across axes.
No variation of label noise. No tuning of regularization: lambda is fixed at 1e-6 and 1e-5. No check for multiple peaks.
The x-axis is never re-expressed as an effective number of parameters.

record.verdict_notes: Tranche is T1 rather than T2 because the MNIST example explicitly replicates an example from Belkin et al., an original source, with near-identical design (random ReLU features, least squares, n=10000). However, it uses small ridge regularization rather than the minimum-norm solution. The polynomial toy example is a new setting. The MNIST result is stated only as 'confirms' with a figure. Results are from a single round, and the authors say they are consistent across repetitions.

versions.untested_parts: The study explicitly restricts its empirical analysis to shallow models; it does not test model-wise double descent in deep networks.
No sweep over training epochs or training time.
No sweep over the number of training samples near the interpolation threshold.
Tests model-size curves in two shallow-model examples, not the full range of model classes.
Examines model size only; does not test whether one measure predicts the peak across epochs and sample size.
Does not test label-noise or variance dependence, multiple peaks, or optimally tuned regularization.
Does not re-express complexity using an effective number of parameters or test whether that makes the curve U-shaped.

rows.subject: toy polynomial regression model
rows.size_stated: p varied; p = 8 sampled points; p = 2 and p = 16 identified as optima for the two bounds
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number p of polynomial terms in a regularized least-squares model.
rows.note: The text describes a U-shaped and double-descent generalization-error curve as p varies.

rows.subject: toy polynomial regression model
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number p of polynomial terms and measured training error.
rows.note: The text says training error decreases to zero up to the interpolation threshold.
rows.check: Training error falling to zero only marks the interpolation threshold; on its own it cannot show the second descent of test risk.

rows.subject: toy polynomial regression model
rows.size_stated: p varied; p = 16 is the stated optimum under the stability-based bound
rows.operation_detail: Estimated algorithmic stability while varying the number p of polynomial terms.
rows.measure: Algorithmic stability H(AH) and its bound
rows.locator: Section 4, Figure 2, fourth graph; accompanying text
rows.note: The authors say stability detects a behavioral change after interpolation and that the stability-based bound selects p = 16.
rows.check: Hypothesis stability is a generalization-bound term. The paper does not use it to predict the location of the peak along size, epochs or samples, which is what V5 says. Moved to fits_no_version.

rows.subject: toy polynomial regression model
rows.size_stated: p varied; p = 2 is the stated optimum under the Rademacher-based bound
rows.operation_detail: Estimated Rademacher complexity while varying the number p of polynomial terms.
rows.measure: Rademacher complexity R(F) and its bound
rows.locator: Section 4, Figure 2, third graph; accompanying text
rows.note: The text says Rademacher complexity only increases with parameter count and its bound selects p = 2, before the second minimum at p = 16.
rows.check: Rademacher complexity rising with p is not an 'opposite effect' for any version. A capacity measure failing to explain the second descent does not challenge V5's claim about effective model complexity. The 'reversed' state is wrong.

rows.subject: MNIST model with random ReLU features
rows.size_stated: p varied; each Vi is sampled from the unit hypersphere in R^28
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number p of random ReLU features in a regularized least-squares classifier.
rows.measure: Test error, estimated as percentage of misclassified samples
rows.note: The authors say Figure 3 confirms the results and comments from Figure 2, including the double-descent behavior.

rows.subject: MNIST model with random ReLU features
rows.operation_detail: Varied the number p of random ReLU features and measured training error.
rows.note: The text says Figure 3 confirms the earlier results; the plotted training-error curve is not numerically tabulated.
rows.check: Training error alone does not measure the double-descent effect on test risk.

rows.subject: MNIST model with random ReLU features
rows.operation_detail: Estimated algorithmic stability while varying the number p of random ReLU features.
rows.measure: Algorithmic stability H(AH) and its bound
rows.note: The authors say Figure 3 confirms the results and comments from Figure 2, including the stability-based account.
rows.check: Same issue as r3. The text only says Figure 3 'confirms' Figure 2. There is no peak-location prediction.

rows.subject: MNIST model with random ReLU features
rows.operation_detail: Estimated Rademacher complexity while varying the number p of random ReLU features.
rows.measure: Rademacher complexity R(F) and its bound
rows.note: The paper's discussion says Rademacher complexity only increases with parameter count and does not capture the over-parameterized behavior.
rows.check: Same issue as r4. The Rademacher comparator does not bear on V5.

relationships.condition: Toy polynomial ridge regression (n=8, lambda=1e-6) and MNIST random-ReLU-feature least squares (n=10000, lambda=1e-5), single run
relationships.reason: Test error shows a U-shape below the interpolation threshold and a second descent above it. For the toy model the second minimum is at p=16 (r1). The authors say MNIST confirms this (r5). Figure-only, with no uncertainty reported.
relationships.display_finding: Test error followed a U-shape below interpolation and declined again above it, with a second polynomial-regression minimum at p=16 and the same pattern reported on MNIST.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
